cells.tense: The effort you carried is visible now, honored by the people who saw it, and you get to stand in what it made.
cells.act: tend the resource with responsible care
cells.ask: Pick whatever is actually growing in your hands — a skill, a person, a place — and give it twenty unhurried minutes, no tally of what comes back.
cells.core:
What you gave up for a long stretch has finally been seen. That is not vanity — it is the natural moment when quiet work becomes acknowledged, and you get to stand inside what it made you. Let it land without performing for it or waving it off.

What keeps this honest is caring for it the way you did when no one was watching. That care was not forced then, and it does not have to exhaust you now. Give the thing genuinely growing in your hands twenty unhurried minutes, no count of what it returns. You will know it is going well when the work feels steady and easy, and the praise is just the effect, not the engine.
cells.sheetLine: What you gave up is visible now. It is still yours.
cells.verb: giving quietly under pressure, then letting what was given for come back visible and honored
cells.place: standing in your own nature as it shows itself, not as it is praised

cells.tense: You are rehearsing a future where the credit finally lands, bracing for a moment that has not arrived.
cells.act: strike one thing from the list that does not serve
cells.ask: Cross off one commitment you are holding mostly so the effort will get noticed — not forever, just off today.
cells.core:
The push to make the cost legible is running ahead of what is here. You want the sacrifice seen, so you pile on — more hours, more proof, more evidence it was worth it. Some of what sits on the pile got there only so there would be something to point at.

When practice is clean it flows without force; solitude connects and the refining serves growth. Test that by crossing one thing off today's list — not the real load, the padding. Notice how the day feels one item lighter. If what remains holds without an audience, it was worth keeping. If it collapses, you have learned what was holding it up.
cells.sheetLine: You are padding the pile so the credit will arrive on schedule.

cells.tense: You gave and nothing came back that way, and you are still standing at a doorway already behind you.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: Take back that piece of work you handed off hoping someone else would finish it or notice, and carry it yourself, all the way.
cells.core:
Waiting has become the stance. You gave, nothing returned, so now you do not step all the way into the room. The part of you that can be seen is still there; it is standing down, waiting on a receipt that is not coming. What is left is the old door, kept open, kept watched.

Steadfastness here is not forcing feeling into what has run dry — it is drawing on what is underneath. Take one piece of your own work back from whoever you left it with and carry it, without tracking whether anyone notices. That charges what ran low. Not to prove they were wrong to overlook you — just to feel your own weight on your own ground again.
cells.sheetLine: You are waiting for someone to hand back what you finished.

cells.tense: You have been giving steadily for a while, and by your own telling you did nothing worth mentioning.
cells.ask: Keep one patch that is yours alone — not your role's, not the group's — and hold that steady for a week, unannounced.
cells.core:
It was never about praise. It started smaller: something you wanted to grow, tended because tending was what you did. Now the same acts hold people up daily and you would say you were not doing anything. That is not modesty — the work is real, and the one doing it left no line in the account.

So go back to the simpler form. Pick a patch that belongs to you rather than your role — ground, a practice, a person you are actually responsible for — and keep only that for a week, quiet. You will know it is working when you can hold it steady and not clutch. What you tend in the open is yours whether or not anyone writes it down.
cells.sheetLine: You do the growing. You would say there is nothing to mention.
